chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Mattie Hite in Atlantic City
summary: Cheatham knew Mattie Hite at the Bellman's Club, where she sang risque songs from table to table.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I remember that name too. But -- the same thing, I didn't come in contact with them.
No, I didn't know Mamie Maime Carter.
Mattie Hite I knew very well.
Well what about -- tell me about her?
Well, I met Mattie Hite in Atlantic City, at the Bellman's Club, that's where Claude Hopkins had the group there.
Oh, she was a very good entertainer. She sang at all tables, you know, from table to table, that
was her style -- the style in those days.

And she would keep the band playing for maybe a couple of hours. Once -- during one song. And she had a lot of -- most of her songs were very risqué. And she'd pick up a lot of money, you know, going from table to table singing these risqué type of songs.
She had a high pitched voice?
Had a pitched -- high pitched type of voice, sort of --
Yes. That's right, yes. Very good entertainer.
